instruments.evidence: Four commits: byte ranges on both content routes, media moved into a src, the tile assertion, and the removal of the playback reduction. Boundaries: the routes -> a player (ranges and cache keys); the app -> the API across an ORIGIN, which is what the whole change turns on; and a shared cache -> two different answers under one URL.
Ledgers 68b74a58a and a053fc7eb, both of this same media path. The second's cache-R3 is why B3 was aimed at what the client actually sends rather than at what the route declares.

instruments.why: No assembled string or provider payload changed.

instruments.evidence: Read the rendered markup for every branch: full image, clip, tile with a thumbnail, tile without, and the retry state. That is where the missing credential mode was visible -- the elements were plain src attributes with no mode at all.

Printed the responses for a whole request and a ranged one on both routes: 200 with Accept-Ranges and the full length, 206 with an inclusive Content-Range and the whole object's size after the slash, 416 with bytes */size. Then asked what a shared cache would store, which is stream-R3.

instruments.why: No query, migration or stored row changed.

instruments.evidence: Nothing model-facing changed. The clips these routes now serve were rendered and watched earlier in this ledger's history; no prompt or provider input is unverified.

Range arithmetic is the constant that had to match across the seam: inclusive at both ends, and the size after the slash is the object's rather than the slice's. Both stated in tests rather than trusted.
The component reads URLs from exported resolvers now instead of Blobs from a service, and the two blob methods that no longer had a caller were removed rather than left as dead exports.

instruments.why: No rule lives in two implementations.

instruments.evidence: The other end of this contract is a browser, and the contract is CORS. Read the server's CORS middleware rather than assuming: it echoes the origin and allows credentials for the app's own origins and, outside production, for any loopback origin. That is what makes the fix for stream-R1 work, and reading it is what showed the fix was needed.

instruments.why: No field added to a struct that crosses a boundary.

instruments.evidence: The fixture that mattered was the API base URL. Tests resolve against http://localhost:8080, which the component's own environment treats as another origin -- exactly as production does under .env.production. Asking what a real browser sends to that origin is what found stream-R1.
The ranges a player really sends: bytes=0- to start, a seek with an open end, both ends, a single byte, and a suffix. All in the table.

A start past the end, a backwards range, a negative start, a non-numeric range, an empty suffix, a zero suffix -- all refused with 416 rather than silently clamped into something plausible. A range must also not become a way to read part of somebody else's clip, which is asserted at the route.
An empty object, a suffix longer than the object, an end past the end, multiple ranges, another unit, and no header at all.
The elements were compared against the fetch they replaced. The fetch said credentials include explicitly; the elements said nothing, which is not the same default. That is stream-R1.
Every branch of serveStoredObject is exercised, including the one for a backend that cannot serve a range.
A 401 on an element cannot run the refresh the fetch wrapper did. That is stated in the file, surfaced to the user, and answered by a retry that asks again rather than replaying a cached failure.

instruments.why: Nothing new is gated on a flag.

instruments.evidence: One helper serves both content routes rather than two copies of range arithmetic. The retry suffix was the opposite -- one value used for two different URLs -- which is stream-R2.

The shape of stream-R1 is 'an element inherits a default the fetch it replaced had stated explicitly'. Looked for others in the same component: loading, decoding and preload are all stated; nothing else relies on an unstated default.
A ranged read holds a file handle and closes it on both paths; the local backend's bounded reader closes the file rather than leaking a descriptor on every seek, which is asserted.
Deleting the playback reduction leaves nothing behind: it wrote to a temp directory it removed, and it never created a stored object.

Three controls built after the commit and replayed. One PASSED at first -- the retry assertion was on the full-size image, where a single suffix is correct by construction -- so the test was rewritten to exercise the tile, where the two URLs genuinely differ, and the control then failed.
Accept-Ranges is what makes a player try to seek at all, and it is asserted on the whole-file answer as well as the partial one. Vary is asserted on both for the same reason.
go build, go vet, gofmt, tsc -b and eslint clean. The handlers package passes with -p 1. Frontend: 159 files, 913 passed, 1 skipped.
No new technique. C4 earned its keep on a contract whose other end is a browser rather than a provider, and C7 on a fixture that was an origin rather than a path.
